assertion: Penelec's price to compare will rise 3.2% in December, increasing from 13.142 cents per kilowatt-hour to 13.564 cents.

assertion: Last December, Penelec's rate rose from 11.004 cents to 11.747 cents per kilowatt-hour, a 6.75% increase.

assertion: The new rate is about 15% higher than Penelec's rate after last year's December change.
independent_value: 13.564/11.747 = +15.5%; 'about 15%' is a fair rounding (could be 15 or 16). Note: most of the gap arose from a mid-year (June) reset, not December.

assertion: For West Penn Power customers, the price to compare will rise from 12.075 cents per kilowatt-hour to 12.386 cents in December.
searched: PUC price to compare December 1 2026 Penelec 13.564 West Penn 12.386

assertion: Last December, West Penn Power's rate increased from 10.318 cents to 10.947 cents per kilowatt-hour.
The new rate is about 13% higher than West Penn Power's rate after last year's December change, even though this year's increase is smaller.
Statewide, nine of 11 utilities raised their rates last December. This year, 10 are raising them.
independent_value: 2025 release: 9 increases (Duquesne, Pike, Met-Ed, Penelec, Penn Power, West Penn, PECO, PPL, Citizens), 2 decreases (Wellsboro, UGI); 2026: 10 of 11

assertion: The PUC said the price changes reflect wholesale market costs, which can include PJM capacity costs.
inaccuracy: PUC release attributes prices to wholesale market rates; it does not mention PJM capacity costs. That addition is the reporter's, though widely supported context.
independent_value: PUC 2026 release says prices 'are based on wholesale market rates'; no PJM text.
